## Change and mathematical scope

Consolidate twelve helper placements in PR610's literal owner map, raising its conditional κ from **0.00162536523418317** to **0.001625434703655052** (**+0.00427408%**). The conservative value is **0.001625434700837327**. The dispatch remains jp8 ×71 / ck ×1; every provider circuit, construction recipe, external source pin and verifier script is unchanged from the pinned PR610 head.

The repair in PR610 leaves several rank-48 owners with one helper. This change moves helpers from different complete calls into fewer owners while preserving the idle windows, capacity and one-helper-per-family-per-call constraints. Twelve records change placement and two additional records change only packed offsets. The standard-library discovery tool reproduces the frozen map and records all twelve moves; its floating-point search objective is not trusted for admission. Exact κ is `406358675913763/250000000000000000`.

**Dependency and review scope:** this is stacked on #610 at `b7c680ea38b9a25a89fce189bb927b45842362d0`, which builds on #604 and #601. Those inherited commits appear in the comparison against main while the dependencies remain unmerged. The numerical change and nomination tool are isolated in [commit c0874b2](https://github.com/jeremydiviney/integer-mult-bounds/commit/c0874b2491382210546a592df0aba8223fee4f9f) (14 files); subsequent updates add validation evidence only. This does not update the repository's selected certificate.

**Concurrent results:** #614–617 and #622 now report stronger κ values. This submission contributes a small reproducible owner-consolidation tool, a verified improvement over pinned PR610, and its replay evidence; it makes no current-record or optimality claim.

Detailed changes and reproduction commands: [OWNER-CONSOLIDATION.md](https://github.com/jeremydiviney/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c0874b2491382210546a592df0aba8223fee4f9f/research/complex-571-cold14/OWNER-CONSOLIDATION.md).

## Validation

- Fresh strict default-SPEC replay: **all 41 stages pass**, with no reused baseline or provider outputs.
- **23 owner mutations** and **114 assembly mutations** rejected; phase and generated-artifact identity controls pass.
- Both exact moment engines and the outer assembly admit the result, including the conservative calculation and rejection of the next endpoints/grid point.
- The nomination, decompressed owner map and twelve-move record regenerate exactly. All inherited verifier scripts and provider recipes are byte-identical to pinned PR610.
- `make gen4-bank-verify`: all nine stages and 112 immutable source pins pass. Full repository `make verify` subsequently passed on submitted head `c0874b2`, including all 84 isolated test modules and historical patch checks; the checkout remained clean.

[Retained replay evidence](https://github.com/jeremydiviney/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a0d472c/research/complex-571-cold14-repacking-audit) contains the result, stage receipt, assembly controls and contributor validation record. This is contributor validation awaiting independent review. The cited PR543 bit supplier is repriced but not rebuilt; the inherited all-size, compiler, hosting, precision and analytic assumptions remain. No unconditional multiplication theorem or full Lean certification is claimed.

Credit remains with DreamingOfClouds (Claude Opus 5.5 assisted) for PR604/PR610's cold-ended providers, dispatch and owner construction; jeremykothe2 and all predecessor contributors retain the detailed attribution in NOTICE.md. This owner consolidation was prepared by Jeremy Diviney with OpenAI Codex assistance.


**Follow-up #624:** our newer owner-repacking contribution builds on the 492-helper construction in #622, with conditional κ = 0.001635425470780892. It also documents the stronger concurrent #623 result.

This proves an exact ceiling for **all 72-call choices of PR615's two native suppliers and all whole-helper packings into its fixed owner capacity inventory**, using the inherited native moment and outer conversion:

`κ < 1628658892827744394867 / 1001628658892827744394867 < 0.001626010676080313339617167`.

The proof relaxes timing and includes fragmented idle capacity. Integer pattern weights and 92 rational inequalities replace the numerical LP optimality claim. Independent enumeration checks all 915 relevant integer multisets. The certificate has no solver or floating-point dependency.

The package also refines PR615's outer output grid from `10^-18` to `10^-24`, certifying **κ = 0.001626010676080313339567**, within `51/10^24` of this family's ceiling. This is only a rounding refinement: the native words, recipes, owner assignment, moments, bootstrap steps and strict outer inequalities are unchanged. The next-grid rejection now tests the next `10^-24` tick.

**This is not a frontier-record claim.** PR617 changes the suppliers and is outside this ceiling. I independently replayed its exact head `904d62855723c00f8acef9a287a10768598fdeb2` with 42 fresh stages and a separate owner-map/moment check, obtaining its higher conditional κ of `0.001635183729255778`. Its separate evidence is not part of this package.

Validation included here:

- Fresh macOS and Linux aarch64 Python 3.14.8 replays: 42 stages each, no baseline/local reuse; 271.526 s and 313.749 s.
- All 43 receipt artifacts and 42 raw stage logs per platform retained and hash-verified, including from the actual committed Git archive.
- Exact ceiling and outer-refinement certificates byte-identical across platforms.
- Five malformed-input controls rejected with Python assertions disabled; seven bootstrap steps, 47 strict outer constraints per model and fine-grid/slack rejection controls independently recomputed.
- Primary verifier byte-identical to PR615; source contracts unchanged. Only two arithmetic expressions change in the inherited runtime. Broad whitespace checks report retained whitespace in pinned inherited sources; new files pass the scoped check.
- A dedicated Python 3.11/3.14 CI workflow is included; CI results are not claimed yet.

Core proof and replay: `research/complex-pr615-ceiling/`. Raw evidence and search provenance: `research/complex-pr615-ceiling-validation/`.

Construction credit belongs to jeremykothe2 (PR615 and predecessors), DreamingOfClouds (PR604 and predecessors), and the earlier contributors retained in NOTICE. The new ceiling, supplemental checks and rounding refinement were prepared with OpenAI Codex. A four-branch fresh-context search selected the refinement; parent research supplied the ceiling. This applies the fork/select/continue method from https://arxiv.org/html/2610.07447v1 without claiming a controlled efficiency experiment.

The ceiling is restricted to these suppliers, this capacity geometry and this moment/outer interface. All-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape/exact recovery, analytic transfer and bit H1-H5 assumptions remain conditional. This is not κ=1, an unconditional multiplication theorem, or a complete Lean proof.

scope.body:
The prior cyclic inverse notes establish finite invertibility at roots of unity. That does not give a conditioning bound independent of the cyclic length. This package proves such a bound for every prime-power kernel order, including dyadic orders, and every primitive root choice.

For `n=r-1`, `D=phi(r)`, and `H=2^r-1`, it proves `|P(z)| >= delta = 1/(2rn H^(nD-1))` on the entire unit circle. For every unit scalar `tau`, cyclic length `L`, and integer shift step `w`, it then proves `||P(tau Z_L^w)^-1||_infinity <= delta^-1 + 2nH/(r delta^2)`. Finite products and unit diagonal gauges retain the stated bound. Radix two has a separate bound of two.

The proof uses integral tail coefficients, prime-power residue reduction, a nonzero Sylvester determinant, paired field embeddings, cofactor bounds, and an absolutely convergent Fourier series. The logarithm of the inverse upper bound is `O(r^2 phi(r))`; no dependency on cyclic length remains.

Validation:
- The written proof passed a separate AI-assisted mathematical review.
- The standard-library engine checks eight exact cyclotomic cases; isolated optimized Python gives the committed deterministic record.
- An independent SymPy engine matches all eight determinants and norms, checks an extra primitive choice, and verifies 36 actual cyclic inverse products. Both engines reject the intended unit-root and omitted-conjugation controls.
- Both engines pass from a relocated standalone package with no historical workspace inputs.
- `make verify` passed on pinned main `5996f9043c27bafa90b23e1c937de92a738f1a76`, including `make gen4-bank-verify`, `make frontier596-verify`, all remaining tests, and patch applicability checks. `git diff --cached --check` passed.

This is a scoped analytic contribution, with **no new integer kappa, complex b, BIT c, or paid inversion algorithm**. Efficient preparation, combined precision and rounded execution, restoration, and tape costs remain open. The scalar theorem uses standard mathematical facts; any multiplication application still needs the original algorithmic interfaces. No all-composite, full multiplication theorem, practical speedup, literature priority, or maintainer acceptance claim is made.

Credits and exact pins are in `SOURCE.json` and `NOTICE.md`: OpenAI's exact-DFT kernel, classical q-Pochhammer/Newton factorization (Alexey Kuznetsov), and prior unpublished local cyclic inverse work. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance during research directed by Ali Romman. Apache-2.0.

scope.body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.00163542231500688**. This is +2.39e-7 (+0.0146%) over our PR617 (0.001635183729255778). The conservative model gives 0.001635422312138865.

This is the first change to the **helper skeleton** itself since the 504-helper raw word. A new atom, **leaver-read K-triangles**, removes 12 helpers per call: **492 instead of 504**. Everything downstream is PR617's construction, rebuilt on the new word: the PR571 prefix and kernels, coalescing, hyperplane ends, PR604/PR617 cold ends and the E1 pair. Dispatch is **jp8 ×65, ck ×7**. The owner RINS ran 1800 s and stopped with a gap of 1e-7.

**The atom.** In today's skeleton, every triangle of faces (Φ_i ± Φ_j)/2 is formed and then copied 3 times before the paired output-basis targets (K-coordinates) read it. On the four (p, −1) triangles, p ∈ {01, 23, 45, 67}, the selected partition contains the pair in all three blocks that contain it. There the faces are **never formed**: each K-coordinate reads its own leaver plus the 4 unformed leavers of the other two faces directly, in a read order found by CP-SAT with no pollution. That saves 3 face copies per triangle, 12 in all.

Two further facts were each checked exhaustively:
- this is the most the atom can give without breaking cold ends;
- the (p, +1) triangles are not used, because their leavers would break PR604's S b.10 cold units.

**The words are rebuilt from pinned sources, not shipped as data.**
- `code/construct_k_triangle.py` is PR531's `construct_504` plus the atom. With an empty schedule it reproduces RAW504's content exactly.
- `build_port_stage.py` carries every downstream recipe across from an in-run shadow of the 504 chain, pinned against it.
- `build_frame_regroup.py` re-coalesces the frames of the 48 rewired K-coordinate reads.
- Every step passes the existing exact native audit (forward and inverse-transpose replay on arbitrary inputs, monotone native frames).

**Verifier change: 504 → R.** The global code had 504 helpers hard-coded. It now reads R from the words; R is pinned independently through SPEC (`hosted_residuals == 72·R`), the owner and plan hashes, the width digest, and `R == 504 − 3·#triangles`. `PROOF-NOTE-R.md` lists all 32 changed sites. A revert control at each site restores the 504 code. On this R = 492 package every R-dependent site **fails** when reverted; only the version label and one parent-bank site pass, as intended. On PR617's 504 package, all 32 revert controls agree, and the generalised code reproduces PR617's global outputs bit-exact. Two coverage items lost in the first port are restored, generalised to R through helper-map images:
- the width-8 spot check;
- the swap control.

The identity control's register is now derived as 2·112+SPOT[2]. It had been hard-coded, which would have crashed at R ≠ 504.

**Independent review: SOUND.** The reviewer:
- re-ran the strict chain (63/63 stages);
- re-ran the revert controls at R = 492 and R = 504;
- checked the empty-schedule reproduction;
- re-audited the 492 raw word with its own independent mod-p and frame check;
- confirmed the 12 removed helpers drop out of every count (716 owners per call, 35424 hosted = 72·492, rank mass 520704) and that the extra target climbs are charged.

The code files in this commit match the reviewed hashes, 23/23.

**Declarative inputs ship in this first commit:**
- `data/WITNESS.json`, which declares R in `geometry.helpers`;
- `data/EXPECTED.json`;
- `data/cand.json`, carrying the solve provenance;
- `data/search/`;
- the proof notes `PROOF-NOTE.md` (the atom section) and `PROOF-NOTE-R.md`.

`data/PLAN.json` is reproduced byte for byte from the solver output.

## Verification

```sh
research/complex-571-cold14-k492/verify.sh /tmp/complex-571-cold14-k492 ..   # SOURCE_ROOT holds worktrees pr568 pr569 pr571 pr575 pr583 at the pinned commits
```

Local result (Windows, CPython 3.11.11): the commit was preflighted from a fresh clone first (committed blobs equal the MANIFEST, every file LF, pin check passes, `spec.py check` OK, code hashes equal the reviewed set 23/23). The official run from that clean clone of `f69477f` then gave `PASS_COLD14_NATIVE_COMPLEX_AND_CITED_BIT`, κ 0.00163542231500688, 64/64 stages exit 0, 483 s, with no reused baseline or locals; every provider word is rebuilt from the pinned sources through `construct_k_triangle.py`. The receipt records MANIFEST sha256 a99f1047…, equal to the committed MANIFEST. Separately, a strict generic verify from `data/WITNESS.json` + `data/EXPECTED.json` passed (63/63 stages, same κ).

GitHub CI has not run, and I make no claim about it.

## Credits

- **DreamingOfClouds**: PR604 (the cold-ended construction, `cold_end`, verifier changes and package), PR599, PR509 and PR516 (Lean).
- **jeremykothe2**: PR617, PR615, PR614, PR609, PR607, PR601, PR600, PR596, PR593, PR592 and PR591 (the hyperplane-end base), and this owner map.
- The pinned PR568, PR569, PR571, PR575 and PR583 packages and all earlier contributors are listed in NOTICE.md.

**AI disclosure and authorship:** Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), running in the omp coding harness, found the K-triangle atom, rebuilt the chain on the 492-helper word, generalised the verifier to R helpers with per-site revert controls, ran the independent review, found the dispatch and owner map, built the declarative inputs and prepared the PR. Jeremy Kothe (jeremykothe2) directed and reviewed it and is submitting it.
